name: Evaluating LLM-based Agents for Multi-Turn Conversations: A Survey (Guan et al.)
venue: ACM Transactions on Intelligent Systems and Technology (ACM TIST) 2025; DOI 10.1145/3793671. First posted arXiv:2503.22458 (28 Mar 2025; v2 revised 5 Jan 2026).
authors_affiliation: Shengyue Guan, Jindong Wang, Jiang Bian, Bin Zhu, Jian-guang Lou, Haoyi Xiong. All authors affiliated with Microsoft (Microsoft Research / Microsoft, China per the camera-ready).
code_url: N/A (this survey has no associated official code repository or released artifact; it is a literature review)
maintained_repo_url: N/A (no maintained GitHub paper list / leaderboard is associated with this survey; the similarly named repo yubol-bobo/Awesome-Multi-Turn-LLMs belongs to a different survey, 'Beyond Single-Turn')
task_domain: Survey of evaluation methods for LLM-based multi-turn conversational agents; spans dialogue/conversation, tool-use/action, memory and context retention, and planning. Not a single-domain method but a meta-level survey covering QA, tool-use, planning, embodied/web agent benchmarks under the multi-turn dialogue umbrella.
problem_setting: Interactive, multi-turn (multi-round) conversational setting where an LLM-based agent integrates dynamic tool use, persistent memory, and sequential planning across turns and sessions, as opposed to isolated single-turn queries. The survey itself is an offline literature analysis (PRISMA-inspired systematic review) rather than an interactive system; it studies how to evaluate such agents. It covers both single- and multi-agent systems and both supervised (annotation-based) and unsupervised (annotation-free / self-judging) evaluation regimes. Literature window 2017-2025 (Transformer era onward), reviewing nearly 250 sources.
what_is_retrieved: N/A as a retrieval method. As a survey, it organizes the literature and (within the surveyed agents) discusses what conversational agents retrieve/recall: dialogue history, retrieved past interactions, tool/API documents, and long-term user preferences/memories. The survey's own 'units' are ~250-350 scholarly papers, benchmarks, metrics, and evaluation methods.
retrieval_grounding: N/A for the survey itself (not a retrieval system). Within surveyed agents, the discussed memory grounding is HYBRID: a static external corpus/tools (docs, APIs) plus a GROWING/episodic memory the agent writes (turn / conversation / permanent memory), with textual forms (complete/recent/retrieved/external interaction) and parametric forms.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: N/A. The survey is not optimizing a retrieval ranking objective. Its evaluation-oriented analog is comprehensiveness: it aims for holistic coverage of evaluation dimensions (what-to-evaluate) and methodologies (how-to-evaluate) rather than a fixed top-k ranking of methods.
retrieval_unit: N/A (survey, not a retrieval method). The survey's units of analysis are scholarly papers, benchmarks/datasets, metrics, and evaluation methods. Within surveyed agents it discusses retrieval units such as dialogue turns, retrieved past interaction segments (cosine/semantic similarity), and tool/API documents.
index_source: N/A. The survey's 'store' is the curated literature corpus assembled via a PRISMA-inspired search (Google Scholar plus venue searches over ICLR, NeurIPS, AAAI, NAACL, EMNLP, ACL, 2022-2024); offline, fixed at review time.
index_structure_topology: N/A as a retrieval index. The survey organizes its corpus via two interrelated taxonomies (hierarchical / tree-structured): a 'what to evaluate' taxonomy (end-to-end experience; action & tool-use; memory; planning) and a 'how to evaluate' taxonomy (annotation-based vs annotation-free, incl. automated metrics, hybrid, and self-judging LLM methods).
retriever_type: N/A (survey performs manual PRISMA-style keyword search + screening, not an automated retriever). Keyword/Boolean search via Google Scholar and venue databases followed by human screening for eligibility.
retriever_learning_signal: N/A (none; off-the-shelf literature search engines plus manual human inclusion/exclusion screening, no learned retriever).
query_construction: N/A. The survey's literature-search 'query' is a fixed set of keywords (e.g. 'evaluation', 'performance assessment', 'benchmark', 'multi-turn/multi-round conversation/dialogue', 'Large Language Model (LLM)', 'LLM-powered/based/agent') applied to Google Scholar and named venues.
query_granularity: N/A. Literature search is one-shot at the corpus level (topic-level keyword query); not a per-step or trajectory-level retrieval.
when_to_retrieve: N/A (one-shot literature collection during the systematic review; the survey itself does not perform iterative or active retrieval).
retrieval_trigger_signal: N/A (fixed schedule: a single PRISMA-inspired collection/screening pass). Within surveyed agents, the survey discusses when-to-retrieve signals for memory (e.g. semantic/contextual relevance, recency thresholds, thought-based retrieval), but this is descriptive of the literature, not the survey's own mechanism.
reranking: N/A. No reranking stage; literature was filtered by manual relevance screening (duplicates removed, then excluded for not focusing on evaluation/agents/benchmarks, then full-text eligibility assessment).
retrieved_context_refinement: N/A. The survey's analog is its multi-stage PRISMA screening/filtering pipeline (dedup, abstract screening, full-text eligibility) that distills 1,123 unique records down to 276 for meta-analysis; not retrieval-context refinement in the RAG sense.
how_retrieved_used: N/A as a method. As a survey, surveyed evidence is used for qualitative synthesis and taxonomy construction (organizing evaluation goals and methodologies, summarizing metrics/benchmarks, and identifying gaps and future directions).
planning_integration: N/A for the survey itself. The survey reviews planning as one of the four 'what to evaluate' components, covering Task Modeling, Task Decomposition (e.g., ADaPT, MLDT, LLM-DP, TDAG), Adaptation and Control, and Reflection (Plan Verification and Plan Selection, e.g., ReAct, Critic-CoT, Self-Refine, MultiESC, DAT, DMPO). It does not itself integrate retrieval with planning.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: N/A (survey does not interleave retrieval with reasoning). It discusses, descriptively, per-turn and per-step evaluation granularity for planning/tool-use within surveyed agents.
retrieved_item_representation: N/A. The synthesized outputs are taxonomies, comparison tables (Table 1 annotation-based vs annotation-free; Tables 2-3 benchmark listings), a PRISMA flow diagram, and a roadmap figure; not injected context.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: N/A. The survey abstracts the literature into high-level taxonomic categories and evaluation dimensions (distilled organizing axes) rather than retrieving raw trajectories or demonstrations.
noise_robustness_mechanism: N/A. The survey's analog is PRISMA-style inclusion/exclusion criteria and human relevance screening to filter out irrelevant/low-quality sources (333 excluded as irrelevant, 267 excluded for lacking focus on LLM-based agent evaluation).
memory_type: N/A for the survey itself. The survey devotes a dimension to evaluating agent memory, taxonomized by Memory Span (turn / conversational / permanent memory) and Memory Forms (textual: complete / recent / retrieved / external interaction; and parametric: fine-tuning and memory-editing). Episodic, retrieval-augmented (e.g., MemoryBank+FAISS), and parametric memory are all covered as subjects of evaluation.
write_back: N/A (survey produces no growing store). Within surveyed agents, write-back to memory (storing new interactions, preferences, insights) is discussed as a capability to evaluate (e.g., Memory Sandbox, experience/insight selectors), but the survey itself does not implement write-back.
online_growth: N/A. The surveyed corpus is fixed after the review. The survey discusses online memory growth (test-time accumulation of context across sessions, e.g., long-term conversation datasets spanning hours to years) as an agent property to evaluate.
write_back_trigger: N/A (never, for the survey itself; it writes no memory). Within surveyed agents, write triggers (per-turn updates, reflective/insight-based storage, recency-based discarding) are described as evaluation targets.
failure_experience_usage: N/A. The survey notes that several reviewed works lack analysis of failure causes and calls for better failure/error-propagation evaluation, but it does not itself store failure experiences.
memory_evolution_update: N/A for the survey. It reviews memory-editing/update techniques (targeted parameter modification, memory management like Memory Sandbox) as agent capabilities to be evaluated.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: N/A (the survey's literature selection is manual PRISMA screening, not a learned/RL policy). It does, however, discuss learned reward models and self-judging LLM evaluators as evaluation methods.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: N/A for the survey. It reviews single-agent and multi-agent dialogue/debate evaluation (e.g., multi-agent data generation, multi-agent task decomposition like TDAG, parliamentary/structured debate benchmarks) but does not itself share memory across agents.
benchmarks: Surveyed (not run by the authors). Representative benchmarks/datasets discussed include: MMLU (Hendrycks et al., 57 tasks), MT-Bench, the LMSYS million-conversation/Chatbot Arena dataset (25 LLMs), MMDU (27 turns), HUMOD (~28,500 dialogues), TopicChat, DailyDialog, MultiWOZ, BotChat, ConvBench, AgentBench, GAIA, ToolBench, MetaTool/ToolE, MTU-Bench, ToolDial, HuggingGPT, API-Bank, MT-Mind2Web, CoSafe (safety/coreference attacks), LoCoMo (long-term memory), LongEval, SocialBench, MemoryBank (with FAISS), DialFact (22k claims), Factcheck-Bench, BELIEF, WikiFactCheck-English.
benchmark_family: QA/multitask (MMLU); dialogue/multi-turn chat (MT-Bench, MMDU, HUMOD, MultiWOZ, BotChat, ConvBench); web/agent (MT-Mind2Web, AgentBench); tool-use (ToolBench, MetaTool/ToolE, MTU-Bench, ToolDial, API-Bank, GAIA, HuggingGPT); memory (LoCoMo, LongEval, SocialBench, MemoryBank); safety (CoSafe); fact-checking (DialFact, Factcheck-Bench, BELIEF, WikiFactCheck-English). The survey groups these by its 'what to evaluate' axes (end-to-end experience, tool-use/action, memory, planning) rather than by RAG benchmark family.
baselines: N/A (a survey reports no head-to-head experimental baselines of its own). For positioning, it contrasts itself against prior surveys: Arora et al., Chang et al. (LLM evaluation), Li (LLM-agent capabilities), Zhang et al. (LLM-as-evaluator/GPT-4), and other dialogue-system surveys, arguing none jointly cover what-to-evaluate and how-to-evaluate for multi-turn agents with agentic-component interactions.
key_metrics: Surveyed evaluation metrics rather than the survey's own results. Covers traditional reference-based metrics (BLEU, ROUGE, perplexity, F1, exact match, accuracy), embedding/model-based metrics (BERTScore), task-completion/success rate, interaction-pattern recognition, memory retention/recall, tool-selection/API-call success rate, hallucination-detection accuracy, and annotation-free / self-judging metrics (LLM-as-a-judge pointwise/pairwise scoring, learned reward-model scores). Categorized into annotation-based vs annotation-free (automated metrics, hybrid human+quantitative, self-judging LLM).
headline_result: N/A (survey, no single experimental headline number). Closest quantitative facts: PRISMA-inspired systematic review of nearly 250 sources (264 references); collected 479 (Google Scholar) + 1,081 (venue) records, 1,123 unique after dedup, 351 included in qualitative synthesis and 276 in meta-analysis; two complementary taxonomies (what-to-evaluate / how-to-evaluate).
ablations: N/A. As a literature survey, it presents no controlled ablations. Its structural analyses instead include the qualitative comparison of annotation-based vs annotation-free evaluation (Table 1) and the PRISMA selection breakdown showing how exclusion criteria reduce the candidate pool.
evaluation_decoupling: N/A for the survey. It does, however, advocate decoupling component-level evaluation (tool-use accuracy, memory retention, planning/decomposition quality) from end-to-end experience evaluation, organizing the field along exactly this intrinsic-vs-end-to-end split.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: N/A as own results. Thematically, the survey argues strongly for process (not just outcome) evaluation: it emphasizes per-turn and interaction-process quality, error propagation across turns, reasoning faithfulness, and intermediate planning/tool-use steps, criticizing benchmarks that score only final outcomes.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: N/A as own measurements. The survey discusses cost/efficiency trade-offs as a theme: annotation-based evaluation is costly/slow (human effort) while annotation-free/self-judging is scalable but incurs per-query LLM API latency/cost and bias; it calls for scalable, real-time, hierarchical evaluation pipelines (fast filters + deeper evaluation) to reduce cost.
context_budget_and_selection_count: N/A. Not applicable to a survey (no injected-context token budget). Related theme: the survey discusses agent memory budget trade-offs (retaining everything vs discarding) and complete-vs-recent-vs-retrieved interaction strategies as evaluation concerns.
survey_scope_and_axes: Two interrelated taxonomies: (1) WHAT to evaluate - end-to-end experience (task completion, multitask capabilities, interaction patterns, user experience & safety), action & tool-use (API interaction/dynamic tool-use, multi-step tool selection & reasoning, reliability/hallucination), memory (memory spans: turn/conversation/permanent; memory forms: textual complete/recent/retrieved/external and parametric), and planning (task modeling, decomposition, adaptation & control, reflection). (2) HOW to evaluate - annotation-based vs annotation-free, including automated metrics, hybrid human+quantitative, and self-judging LLM methods. PRISMA-inspired methodology over literature from 2017-2025; ~264 references (cited as 'nearly 250 sources'); collected 1,560 records -> 1,123 unique -> 351 qualitative-synthesis -> 276 meta-analysis. Sources span peer-reviewed conference (~40%), journal (~25%), preprint (~20%), industry reports (~15%).
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (this is a survey, not a benchmark). It catalogs others' benchmarks in Tables 2-3 (multitask/interaction/temporal/safety/tool-use, and reliability/next-turn/query-rewrite/memory/task-representation/decomposition/plan-selection) but constructs no new dataset.
builds_on: Methodologically builds on the PRISMA systematic-review protocol (Page et al. / Moher et al.). Conceptually grounded in the agent paradigm (planning, tool-use, memory) and standard NLG/dialogue evaluation (BLEU, ROUGE, perplexity, BERTScore) and LLM-as-a-judge / reward-model evaluation literature (e.g., MT-Bench, Chatbot Arena).
contrasts_with: Positions itself against prior surveys that leave gaps: Arora et al. (brief dialogue-system overview), task-oriented vs non-task-oriented dialogue classifications that overlook agent-system interaction, Li (LLM-agent capabilities without multi-turn focus), Chang et al. (broad LLM evaluation without multi-turn specifics), Zhang et al. (LLM-as-evaluator without detailed annotation-based vs annotation-free treatment), and several recent perspective surveys that ignore inter-component interactions and multi-turn-specific challenges.
lineage: Surveys lineage: a meta-level survey of evaluation methodology for LLM-based multi-turn conversational agents. It sits alongside other agent/RAG/evaluation surveys, uniquely organizing the field via dual what-to-evaluate / how-to-evaluate taxonomies and covering memory, tool-use, and planning components jointly within the multi-turn dialogue setting.
explicit_cbr_grounding: false - the survey does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza or Kolodner.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (survey, not a tool-retrieval method). It reviews tool-use evaluation benchmarks (ToolBench, MetaTool, MTU-Bench, ToolDial, API-Bank, GAIA) but does not engineer tool documents/embeddings.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A. The survey discusses dynamic/real-time tool use and document retrieval (e.g., Gorilla-style real-time API documentation retrieval, ToolBench/RapidAPI) as evaluation subjects, but implements no live tool index or protocol itself.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A as a mechanism. The survey notes the importance of multi-step tool chaining and sequential ordering of tools across turns (chain of execution) as an evaluation dimension, but does not model inter-tool dependencies itself.
